questions.q: The LLM is created with temperature=0. What does that do?
options: Makes the output deterministic and focused
Makes the output more random and creative
Doubles the model's context window size
Turns off the model's safety filters
questions.explain: temperature=0 makes the model pick the most likely tokens — consistent, focused answers.

questions.q: What happens if you raise the temperature toward 1?
options: The answers become perfectly deterministic
The answers get more random and varied
The retriever returns more document chunks
The embedding dimension increases
questions.explain: Higher temperature = more randomness/creativity; lower = more focused and repeatable.

questions.q: max_retries=1 and timeout=25 on the LLM do what?
options: Set the chunk size and the overlap values
Choose the embedding model's dimension
Limit API retries and cap the request time
Control how many chunks are retrieved
questions.explain: They cap how many times a failed call retries and how long a request may run.

questions.q: chunk_size=1000 in the splitter sets what?
options: The number of documents to load into memory
How many chunks the retriever returns
The dimension of the embedding vector
The length of each text piece in characters
questions.explain: chunk_size is how big each text piece is before it gets embedded.

questions.q: What does chunk_overlap=150 do?
options: Repeats text between chunks so context isn't cut
Removes 150 duplicate documents from the set
Limits each answer to 150 characters long
Sets how many chunks are retrieved per query
questions.explain: Overlap repeats a little text at boundaries so an idea split across chunks stays whole.

questions.q: What does RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter do?
options: Turns each chunk into a meaning vector
Splits documents into smaller text chunks
Ranks the retrieved chunks by relevance
Removes stopwords from the document text
questions.explain: It's the tool that breaks documents into chunks before embedding.

questions.q: What is an embedding (text-embedding-3-small)?
options: A compressed zip copy of the document
The English translation of the text
A vector of numbers that captures meaning
A random id assigned to each chunk
questions.explain: An embedding turns text into a numeric vector so meaning can be compared.

questions.q: Why embed the text instead of keyword search?
options: It makes the documents load much faster
It removes the need for a vector database
It only works on images, not on text
It matches by meaning, not by exact words
questions.explain: Embeddings enable semantic search — matching meaning even when the words differ.

questions.q: The retriever uses search_type='mmr'. What is MMR?
options: Retrieval balancing relevance and diversity
A model that writes the final answer text
A method to compress the embedding vectors
A tool that searches the public internet
questions.explain: MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) picks chunks that are relevant AND not redundant.

questions.q: In the retriever, k=8 means what?
options: Eight documents are loaded from the disk
Eight chunks are returned as the context
The model may retry up to eight times
Each chunk is eight sentences long
questions.explain: k is how many chunks the retriever hands to the generator.

questions.q: What does fetch_k=24 do in MMR?
options: Sets the final answer to 24 words long
Retries the whole search up to 24 times
Fetches 24 candidates before narrowing to k
Makes each chunk exactly 24 characters
questions.explain: MMR first fetches fetch_k candidates, then selects the best diverse k from them.

questions.q: lambda_mult=0.5 in MMR controls what?
options: The learning rate used during training
The temperature of the generation model
The number of documents to ingest
The balance between relevance and diversity
questions.explain: lambda_mult tunes MMR: near 1 = pure relevance, near 0 = maximum diversity.

questions.q: The code uses Distance.COSINE. What does cosine measure?
options: Similarity by the angle between two vectors
The exact number of shared keywords
The file-size difference of two documents
The time taken to embed the text
questions.explain: Cosine similarity compares the angle between vectors — closer angle = more similar.

questions.q: What is Qdrant in this project?
options: The language model that writes answers
A vector database that stores embeddings
The web-search tool used for fallback
The library that reads the PDF files
questions.explain: Qdrant stores the embeddings and finds the ones nearest to a query.

questions.q: VectorParams(size=dim) sets what?
options: The maximum number of chunks to store
The temperature of the embedding model
The dimension of the embedding vectors
The number of retries on a failure
questions.explain: size is the embedding dimension (e.g. 768 for Gemini, 1536 for OpenAI).

questions.q: Embedded mode uses a path; the other uses a URL. The difference?
options: Text search vs image search only
The free tier vs the paid tier only
OpenAI vs Gemini embeddings only
A local file store vs a remote server
questions.explain: path = embedded local Qdrant (no server); url = a remote/cloud Qdrant server.

questions.q: What does LangGraph's StateGraph build?
options: The agent's decision graph of nodes and edges
The vector database that stores the chunks
The PDF loader that extracts the text
The embedding model used for the search
questions.explain: StateGraph wires the nodes (retrieve, grade, generate…) and the routing between them.

questions.q: What does the grade_documents node do?
options: Writes the final answer from the chunks
Grades each passage and drops the weak ones
Splits the documents into small chunks
Turns the passages into embedding vectors
questions.explain: An LLM grades each retrieved passage and keeps only the relevant ones.

questions.q: When does the agent fall back to web search?
options: On every single question by default
Whenever the final answer is too long
Only when no relevant documents are found
Only when the temperature is set high
questions.explain: route_after_grade sends it to web search only if zero documents survive grading.

questions.q: What does the hallucination check verify?
options: Whether the question is written in English
Whether the documents loaded correctly
Whether the vectors have the right size
Whether the answer is grounded in the docs
questions.explain: It checks that every claim in the answer is supported by the retrieved passages.

questions.q: Why use with_structured_output for the graders?
options: To force a fixed schema like a yes/no grade
To make the answers longer and richer
To translate the whole output into Uzbek text
To skip the retrieval step entirely
questions.explain: Structured output makes the grader return a clean, parseable verdict every time.

questions.q: The code stores '[Image] ' + caption. What is it doing?
options: Deleting all the images from the PDF
Describing images so they become searchable
Compressing the images to save disk space
Converting the images into audio files
questions.explain: Images are captioned by a vision model so their content can be retrieved like text.
